title: Understanding N-gram Limitations
text: Consider how N-grams capture sequences. They don't account for the biological significance of codons, which are specific sequences of three consecutive letters.

title: Non-consecutive Segments
text: N-grams can capture sequences that are not biologically relevant, such as non-consecutive letters forming a 'word'.

title: Meaningless Segments
text: Segments with fewer than three letters do not correspond to any meaningful biological unit, yet N-grams would still treat them as valid 'words'.

title: Overlapping Segments
text: N-grams can create overlapping segments, which may not align with the biological interpretation of codons.

title: Wrap-around Segments
text: N-grams might incorrectly capture sequences that 'wrap around' the end of a string, which is not possible in DNA sequences.
